correctness.rationale: All 46656 strict labeled profiles are exhaustively evaluated with two independently organized Gale–Shapley implementations that agree profile by profile. Proposal count equals the sum of men-optimal partner ranks, and all six perfect matchings are independently tested for stability. Exact rational recomputation verifies the full distributions, moments, joint table, and conditional means. Published one-round and stable-count marginals match the corresponding verifier outputs.

evidence: Wilson 1972 is the classical proposal-count running-time analysis for random stable marriage.
The 2014 communication-complexity paper summarizes quadratic worst-case and order n log n average behavior under independent uniform preferences.
The 2024 sequence paper gives the exact one-round count and exact marginal number-of-stable-matchings census for n=3.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Asymptotic expectation bounds and one-round enumeration do not determine the complete finite proposal distribution, rank-multiset law, or its coupling to stable-set multiplicity. The new claim is therefore a finer finite calibration rather than a restatement of the classical running-time theory.

value.rationale: Proposal count is the canonical execution-cost statistic for Gale–Shapley and underlies its classical random-input complexity theory. The exact three-by-three law provides a natural finite calibration, identifies the sharp support endpoint, connects runtime directly to men-optimal welfare ranks, and shows how execution cost couples to stable-set multiplicity. These are motivated structural invariants rather than an arbitrary slice.
